# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, well-supported foundation
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to avoid prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, clone, build, install the application, and clean up in a single layer
# This minimizes image size and keeps the image clean.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        build-essential \
        ca-certificates \
        git \
        openmpi-bin \
        libopenmpi-dev && \
    # Clone the latest branch of the AMG (amg2023) repository
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /opt/amg-src && \
    # CORRECTED: Navigate into the root source directory to build libraries and executable
    cd /opt/amg-src && \
    # CORRECTED: Compile the application using the root Makefile which handles dependencies first
    make && \
    # CORRECTED: Copy the compiled executable from its build location to a system location on the PATH
    cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg && \
    # Clean up the build environment to reduce final image size
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/amg-src && \
    apt-get purge -y build-essential git libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get autoremove -y && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments and to allow running as root
# This is critical for compatibility with orchestrators like Kubernetes
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Disable shared memory mechanisms that can cause issues in containers
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
# Exclude InfiniBand, as this is a CPU-only environment
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl="^openib"
# Exclude loopback and docker bridge network interfaces from MPI communication
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude="lo,docker0"

# Set a working directory for application data
WORKDIR /data

# Default command to verify MPI installation. This can be overridden at runtime.
# Example: docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 amg -n 100 100 100
CMD ["mpirun", "--version"]

# MiniCluster manifest for running AMG2023 on an AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes.
# This configuration is designed for a small-scale test run.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: amg2023-test-aws-cpu
  # The Kubernetes namespace where the MiniCluster will be created.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods to create for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The number of tasks (processes) to run.
  # This should typically align with the number of available CPU cores.
  # Set to 4 as a minimum for testing.
  tasks: 4

  # Defines the application container to be run within the Flux cluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute. The Flux operator will automatically wrap this
      # with 'flux run' or 'flux submit'.
      # Runs AMG with problem type 2 and a small grid size of 4x4x4.
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
      
      # The main container is not the launcher pod.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the manifest.
    strict: true

  # Set to false to prevent the job's pods and resources from being
  # deleted upon completion, which is useful for debugging.
  cleanup: false

manager.name: Build and Deploy AMG2023
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.details: Clone the latest branch of amg2023. You MUST put amg on the PATH.

context.optimize:
Maximize the amg2023 figure of merit. You MUST maximize memory per CPU core. More cores are better.
The trick to optimizing this is THREADING. You MUST force OpenMP and any math libraries to use only one thread per MPI rank. On example is setting OMP_NUM_THREADS to "1". You might also consider setting OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism to "cma" as a conservative builder will set to none.
YOU MUST SLOWLY increase the problem size, one dimension at a time, by an increment no more than double the current to increase the FOM. A timeout may not require a smaller problem size but rather a different instance.
A previous run example that has worked well:
  amg -problem 2 -n 128 128 128 -P 8 4 1 on m7g.16xlarge with FOM 8.039496e+08
The size of the MiniCluster MUST be 1. Tasks MUST be at least 4.
To reduce noise in logging, you can set logging.quiet to true.
context.resources:
The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. For your optimization you can choose from the following instance types, and you will need to add the correct nodeSelector with the node.kubernetes.io/instance-type label indicating your choice. You are still limited to one node.      
  c7a.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, AMD
  hpc7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  c6in.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
  r7iz.8xlarge, 16 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6g.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton2)
  t3a.2xlarge, 4 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, AMD
  t3.2xlarge, 4 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6id.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, Intel
  c6id.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 96 GiB Memory, Intel
  t4g.2xlarge, 8 CPU, 32 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton2)
  m6i.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, Intel
  m6a.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 192 GiB Memory, AMD
  m7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  c6i.16xlarge, 32 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, Intel
  c6a.16xlarge, 32 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, AMD
  c7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  r6i.8xlarge, 16 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  r6a.12xlarge, 24 CPU, 384 GiB Memory, AMD
  r7g.12xlarge, 48 CPU, 384 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
  i4i.8xlarge, 16 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, Intel
  d3.4xlarge, 8 CPU, 128 GiB Memory, Intel 
If you choose an ARM (Graviton) instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9. Otherwise, do not change or set it.
If you are using an ARM instance you MUST also set flux.arch: "arm".
context.testing:
You MUST run AMG -problem 2. For testing choose a small problem size no greater than 4 in any dimension.    
If you see a nodeSelector and larger size in the manifest it is OK to keep that and try to debug the issue.
context.details:
You MUST run on only one node. The size of the MiniCluster MUST be 1 and tasks MUST be at least 4.
You MUST NOT oversubscribe.
